result.title: Interrogation Protocols for AI Control
result.comment: 26 pages (8 main + references and appendix), 21 figures, 4 tables. Under review. Code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/interrogation-protocols-A11B/
result.summary: As the intelligence of an AI agent increases relative to a trusted monitor, so does the risk that the monitor will fail to understand the agent's actions or to evaluate them confidently. We introduce interrogation protocols to a high-stakes AI control setting, and allow the monitor to ask the untrusted agent questions about confusing actions. For interrogation to improve safety, a weaker model must be able to distinguish misleading explanations produced by an attack policy from genuine ones produced by an honest policy. We find that on a held-out subset of BashArena, an interrogation protocol improves safety at a 1% audit budget from 72.6% for an actions-only baseline, which does not use interrogations, to 79.5% (+7.0 pp [+0.9, +20.1], 95% paired bootstrap interval), but most of this uplift can be captured by having a trusted model state a specific concern. More broadly, our work suggests that interrogating agents can improve safety, allowing monitors to catch more attacks at a larger capability gap.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将「审问协议」引入高风险的 AI control 场景：由能力较弱的可信监控者就不明所以的动作向不可信智能体追问，并在 BashArena 的留出子集上检验追问能否在 1% 审计预算下提升安全性，同时与「可信模型直接陈述具体疑虑」的对照比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是弱验证者借提问区分诚实解释与误导解释并据此做出审计决策，可能与 LVR 中如何核查答案所依据的视觉证据、判断解释是否忠实以及外部验证成本的问题形成类比，具体可迁移性尚待核查。
